quest.title: A Tower Unto Wisdom and Folly
quest.description: The current crisis is now beyond the capacity of ordinary men, and an unprecedented war is about to begin in the nation of wisdom. But even so, no one is abandoning their post.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act X
chapter.title: Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution

talks.objective: Talk to Alhaitham and Kaveh

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: To what extent we can implement the final plan depends on how successfully the Akasha can be modified and configured. And to make sure the configuration works, Aaru will also need some further optimization.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah, no surprises there.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Once we roll this out, any Sumeru citizens who already have Akasha Terminals can simply continue to use their existing devices.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: This still leaves us with a significant equipment shortage, though. Many groups of people were never issued Akasha Terminals, including mercenaries, the desert folk, and many others.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We'll need a supply of rare materials for the renovation of Aaru and the production of new terminals. Right now, the best place to source these locally is from the Primal Constructs within King Deshret's Mausoleum.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Time is not on our side here. It's gonna be a race against the clock.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: The Aaru merge and renovation project will have to be carried out by you two. Everything's riding on this, so failure is not an option... *sigh* Best of luck to you both.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: As discussed, General Mahamatra Cyno and Mr. Hat Guy will source the required materials.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Mr. Sethos is quite familiar with the layout of King Deshret's Mausoleum. With him accompanying them, things should go quite smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I have every confidence. In the meantime, we may as well take a breather.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Makes sense. There's not much we can do until the materials arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Get in formation and stay close!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What is this, boot camp? Knock it off.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: It's just Cyno being Cyno. You know what he's like.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Everyone clear on our mission objective? Locate the excess Primal Constructs, dismantle them, and extract the required materials.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: And King Deshret's Seven Pillars agreed to this?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If they're just sitting there doing nothing, we might as well put them to use. Thoth's words, not mine.

talks.objective: Collect the materials needed from inside the mausoleum

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Feel free to mingle if you'd like some time to catch up with people. Just remember to get a good night's sleep when you're done — tomorrow is a very important day.

talks.objective: Collect the materials needed from inside the mausoleum
Collect the materials needed from inside the mausoleum
Collect the materials needed from inside the mausoleum
Talk to everyone

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: How many do we need again?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Enough to make an Akasha Terminal for everyone who doesn't own one.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I remember you telling me how revolutionary these Akasha Terminals were. You've used one before, right?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Akademiya declared the Akasha to be the most powerful and comprehensive wisdom dissemination system in history. That should give you an idea of how powerful it is.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Certainly sounds impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Neither Hat Guy nor I have ever had an Akasha Terminal.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Well, if it all goes to plan, that's about to change.

talks.objective: Talk to everyone

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh, goody! Thank you so much for handling the delivery! What a long way it was... You've really outdone yourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I'm well aware what a bumpy, dangerous journey it must have been... Now, I would have loved to oversee the process myself. But of course, those of us who know the plan can't leave the mausoleum.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Oh, trust me, I'm patting myself on the back for my assembly work here. Simply flawless work.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: But will you really be needing all of this?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: According to our plan, yes, this is the quantity required. I have no complaints about the quality either... *sigh* Only the price.... So expensive, ahhh...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I heard you covered a lot of the funding out of your own pocket.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh, that's an exaggeration. The Akademiya provided most of the funds, I just offered a small token of my goodwill.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Of course, the real tragedy is how little profit I'm making on this... *sigh* You know it's a serious crisis when you can't even make money out of it.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: It's really quite a beautiful design. And I'm intrigued by how such a diminutive device is able to output the power of the Light Realm...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Did you attend the lecture on Light Realm energy, Madame Faruzan? I don't believe I saw you there.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Of course I attended! I was just a little late, so I had to listen to the whole thing from outside the back door... Ahem!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Anyway, I have a perfectly good understanding of Light Realm, Elemental, and Abyssal energy, as well as the relationship between the three!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Good to know.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Master told me in private that the conversion process between Light Realm energy and Elemental Energy involves highly classified knowledge that shouldn't be disseminated too widely. But even so, the scholars still shared said information.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hehe, well, you can't enforce a rule that everyone breaks! Is that the idea?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: At first, the Dendro Archon was reluctant to explain it in great depth for safety reasons. Later, she came to terms with it and simply informed my master that we would all have to face the question of survival together.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: To protect someone from such dangers means keeping them in the dark, but for someone to know and embody the wisdom within, they must understand its very essence.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's an information hazard — we're exposed to danger just by knowing the facts... And just like bait, it lures us in by offering us the solution to our problems, but if you're not careful you'll end up pursuing it down a dark path.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: A tricky problem. But today, this big problem has been broken down into many smaller, more trivial ones.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ah, I get it. For instance, you and I share secret knowledge, while she and I take on the risks of life, death, and fate... something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hey, what!? That is not what I call a trivial problem!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, as they often say in Vahumana, an event that is monumental to the individual is negligible in the grand scheme of history. Generally, the fate of the individual is an insignificant affair.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Being from Amurta, where the subject of our research tends to be a lot more personal, I have to disagree. It's hard to dismiss the individual as insignificant.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: In other words, the big problem of survival has been broken down into many small, interconnected factors, and each one of us represents one of those factors?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: When the same secret is shared with a group of people, the same fate binds them together.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: ...Most people would find this unimaginable. But to us scholars, this is the path that has always beckoned to us.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sharing knowledge is a good way to fight against fate. I will always believe in that.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, I think that's everything.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Mm, thanks a lot! But don't go anywhere just yet — I'll still be needing you to calibrate the equipment.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Once everything's ready, I'll need you to lead a team to get it all shipped to King Deshret's Mausoleum.

talks.objective: Inventory the materials and start the modification

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Okay, the materials are ready. We can proceed with the next phase.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alhaitham, how are you getting along?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...Most of the information in Aaru is written in ancient desert scripts. Some of this is written in a tribal language, while other parts seem to be a variant of an oasis script, based on the glyph forms.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh... Not lost to history, I hope?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Some are. All we can do is infer the meaning based on the rules of related languages.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Although... this section actually fills in some of the missing historical record. I'm transcribing it so we can bring it back to the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: After Aaru started up, two more lines of text appeared here. Can you read them?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "Humans may not 'read' what is written by the gods, except by not reading."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "Victory should not be easy to attain, for it symbolizes divine wisdom. Knowledge must not waver, for it has external borders."

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Is this a clue to solving a puzzle? Or is it being symbolic...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You can't read it unless you don't read it... Victory is wisdom, knowledge is confined by borders...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wait, I think I've got it. It's a metaphor, isn't it? It's talking about...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...A chessboard.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: You were right. The youth of today are skilled at solving riddles.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ha, have the secrets buried in the desert not been unearthed over the years all the same? Since Aaru is a place reachable through wisdom, this day was bound to come sooner or later.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Ugh... I've always been against overly cryptic sentences. Don't you get tired of reading and writing all that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you three! Just in time. We've been delving deep into Aaru, and now this board has appeared.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I've heard this was how you'd while away your free hours. You must be quite the experts by now, in that case.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: It is true. King Deshret's chess games are some of the most well-loved of all his wonderful creations. If you have ever been to Safhe Shatranj, you may well be familiar with the chess pieces you see here.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Is this chessboard supposed to be another visualization of the interior of Aaru, then?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Visitors, everything is ready. Only by completing the challenge on the board in accordance with the rules will you be permitted to overwrite Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: One second... It's not... dangerous, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Dangerous? Why yes, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I should be the one to go, then. Wait for me here.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Sounds like the self-confidence of our present company has rubbed off on you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Don't be ridiculous! I'm your upperclassman, and that means I have to look out for you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I appreciate the sentiment. But a game of chess typically requires two players.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Besides, I'm sure they won't let things get out of hand. Keeping things relatively safe is in your best interests too, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Fair enough. I mean, you guys are controlling the difficulty, so please don't go too hard on us, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ah, but Bennu said he wanted to "put some respect into these whippersnappers"... *sigh* Alright, alright.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Thank you! Obviously, we'll still try to be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: This doesn't seem like ordinary chess. Is the goal to defeat the opponent?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: No, you must enter the board and pass the trials we have placed there.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Ready?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Let's do it.

talks.objective: Clear the first stage of the challenge
Clear the first stage of the challenge

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Something on your mind, Miss Nefer?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Nothing in particular. It's just... right now, the future feels strange and unfamiliar.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: But the future has not yet arrived. How can you say how it feels?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Some people know that there's an impending disaster, others remain blissfully unaware. Each group is imagining an entirely different future while walking towards the same one, but when they get there, they'll still find they feel differently about it.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: People are shaped by their circumstances. Different circumstances create people with different perspectives.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I've always found the perspective of the Vahumana Darshan to be a particularly incisive one.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Even at the height of the crisis in Nod-Krai, people held diverging opinions. But things are different this time...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Regardless of faith, gender, wealth, skin color, or eye color, everyone in Sumeru knows what will happen tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The world has never been an especially fair place. Yet now, against all odds, a moment of unprecedented unity and equality is about to take place... It's fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...If only my father could have lived to see this era.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: "Era..." To me, that term represents a much greater span of time. It can be an unsettling word... I would even say I'm afraid of it.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Do angels even feel fear?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes. At least, I do. I fear the gap that grows wider with each passing day, and the never-ending flow of time...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Time renders all memories insignificant, and reduces all splendor to nothing. But those memories are the one thing I do not want to lose.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're very human in that regard.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: If angels draw too close to humanity, our wings burn away in the bright flame of awareness, and we fall to the earth. After spending so long among humans, I have lost much of my former glory.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Maybe that's a good thing.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're more human than some humans are.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I've been talking to Collei a lot in recent days. We seem to be in completely opposite situations. I suppose that makes us good case studies for comparison?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Case studies for who?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: ...Myself, I suppose. After comparing the two of us, I suddenly discovered that I desired more than before.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It was a gentle, pleasant sensation... Just as most people pursue glory and miracles, I too am pursuing miracles of my own.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Guiding humans to make the miracles in their hearts a reality... that is my miracle.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hehe, it doesn't sound so bad, does it?

talks.objective: Clear the second stage of the challenge
Clear the second stage of the challenge

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Mausoleum of King Deshret, Middle-Level

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave

Clear the third stage of the challenge

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Mausoleum of King Deshret, Entrance

talks.objective: Review the match

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Done.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Phew, finally. It's over...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: But seriously, that was incredible! Standing on the chessboard felt completely different from standing on solid ground. And also...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Oh, sorry — I'll save my thoughts for later. Thanks to the three of you for helping us out with this. Is it just me, or were you giving us quite a lot of guidance along the way?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: We made but a humble contribution.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: You lived up to our expectations. Bravo! Our aid was not given for naught.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In addition to the existing functions, I'd like to ask you for another favor.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Since Aaru's interference shield can cover the entirety of the mausoleum, it should be possible to extend its range even further. Perhaps you can find a way.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So, building upon the existing functions to... Ah, I'm with you!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Imagine for a moment: What would the ideal outcome look like if this function were compatible with the devices?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Me oh my. Well, since you ask so very nicely, I suppose... Goatie, Croco, what do you say?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I agree — this is the best solution possible. Please, everyone, we beg you to help us.

talks.objective: Talk to Nahida

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There you are.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Miss Nicole truly is an angel. She shows great wisdom in guiding others, and she has already sent word to Natlan on our behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: She said that while the other members of the Hexenzirkel are busy with important work, she is quite free, and she's more than willing to accompany the people of Sumeru for the entire journey.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's Nicole, alright! Always super patient and loves to help everyone out. Hehe, she's the best.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: She is. So kind and enthusiastic.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, time for us to get going. Let's head out.

talks.objective: Head to the border

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This should be one of the closest places to Natlan in all of Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's the barrier Nicole and Nefer mentioned. It completely cuts this nation off from the others...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But why? Why separate you from the rest of the world now, specifically?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And if I'm not mistaken... Irminsul was polluted once before, wasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I think that's right? The forbidden knowledge was eliminated, but the fact that Irminsul was polluted should remain unchanged.)
Good question. I'm wondering the same thing myself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That voice... Mavuika! You got here pretty quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #Hello, {NICKNAME}. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hello there.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hello, Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mavuika, I apologize for asking you to meet at the border on such short notice.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #I also apologize for not being able to greet you in person. The form in which you see me now is one carried by {NICKNAME}. The real me is inside the Mausoleum of King Deshret, and I am reaching out to you with my mind from here.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Irminsul has been infiltrated by The Doctor. We must be on our guard, as he can spy on information in the world from within the tree. Fortunately, there is no record of {NICKNAME} in Irminsul, and you are still within Natlan's borders.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: My records will be preserved in the Night Kingdom rather than the Ley Lines. As long as the Night Kingdom remains disconnected from the Ley Line cycle, The Doctor has no way of knowing my movements.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So by meeting each other in this way, the meeting essentially never happened.... No wonder Paimon didn't come. You were concerned that her activity would be recorded by Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The Natlanese have heard about the situation in Sumeru. With the borders sealed off, merchants have been forced to stop their shipments... It's pretty serious, and you're the ones bearing the brunt of it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'd like to address the question you raised at the beginning. I can offer a brief explanation, although it will sound rather cruel.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hm...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I don't reach this conclusion gladly, but... Irminsul predates the Heavenly Principles. It existed long ago, when the dragons of Natlan were at the height of their power.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So even when the people of Sumeru became ill because of pollution, it was not a critical issue from the perspective of Irminsul itself. As long as it continues to function normally, the barrier will not be activated.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But this time, The Doctor's invasion has directly affected the tree. That is what caused the barrier to deploy.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Heavenly Principles established a rule that when Irminsul is plunged into grave danger, a portion of power will be reserved to isolate Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That way, even if Sumeru is destroyed, the outside world at least has some time to catch its breath.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We'd certainly need it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Heavenly Principles created almost everything that exists in Teyvat today. To them, preserving the existence of the world and its inhabitants takes priority over protecting Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Heh. Meaning, protecting Sumeru now falls to you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. My own power may be limited, especially compared to yours, but that doesn't mean that we're just gonna sit around and wait for the end. If necessary, I will utilize any and every means at my disposal.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Nicole of the Hexenzirkel didn't say exactly what this meeting was about, but after hearing everything you've said so far... I think I can guess where this is going.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right. Nahida and I discussed it at length. We both know how presumptuous this is, but...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You need the Pyro Gnosis, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. You guessed correctly.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Originally, I only intended to borrow it, but the situation is far graver than I foresaw... So instead, what I ask of you is... to please give the Pyro Gnosis to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hahaha, why do you sound so nervous? There's no need to be shy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Surely a Gnosis is pretty important to a god?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I guess... but it's not as if losing it would suddenly render us powerless.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But I'm sure you don't need me to tell you that. With all the nations you've traveled to and all the gods you've met, you must have realized that by now.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: As far as I'm concerned, a Gnosis is basically an Elemental energy enhancer. But I don't usually use it. You know me... I like to think I'm pretty strong without it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah... not about to dispute that.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Haha. So you see? You don't need to sweat it. Here, take the Pyro Gnosis.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Just like that?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Uh-huh, just like that. To tell the truth, I've always toyed with the idea of giving it to someone who needs it more than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I know you accompanied Nahida here to try and increase the chance of success. It's a good thing you did, because your involvement is one of the main reasons you've managed to persuade me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you sure about this? Handing over your Gnosis just because of me...?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I won't try to quantify it, but trust me — handing over the Gnosis to Tumaini is far from the craziest idea I can think of.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Besides, even if you hadn't come here personally, I think I still would've agreed to Nahida's request.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Irminsul doesn't just affect Sumeru. It impacts all of Teyvat. I know all too well how difficult it can be to protect the things you care about... So logically, morally, or however you wanna cut it, helping you is the right thing to do.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You don't need to tell me the specifics of your plan. Where the Gnosis is involved, the tighter the secrecy, the higher your chances of success.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mavuika...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: My heartfelt thanks go to you and the people of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hehe. Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hmm, but now for the hard part — how do I actually give it to you? The Irminsul barrier is right in the way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have an idea...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Just as I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Huh, incredible... What did you do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just made a lucky guess. This seems to happen quite a lot — things that apply to everyone else don't seem to apply to me. I figured the same might be true here.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Irminsul usually produces effects based on the records it holds. Since {NICKNAME} is a Descender, Irminsul contains no records of {M#him}{F#her}, and thus has no way to impede {M#him}{F#her}.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Haha, is that right... You really are full of surprises.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Catch.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Mavuika. Thank you for trusting us with something so important.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, no need to get so formal. It's not like we're strangers.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #Besides, there's still one problem... You might be able to pass through the barrier, but I don't know about the Gnosis... Any other surprises for us, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Um... Let me try something.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I have the Pyro Gnosis in my hand... It feels strangely ordinary. Not particularly heavy. And yet, this tiny thing symbolizes the mighty authority of a god...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I need to think hard about my memories of Pyro... my memories of journeying through Natlan... All those important experiences I've had.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #The Gnosis disappeared... {NICKNAME}, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Pyro Gnosis disappeared into my body, just like... phlogiston?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe it resonates with you because you've mastered the power of phlogiston. You might not be recorded in the Ley Lines, but you're still our Tumaini.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Whew.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Amazing. I made it back through with the Gnosis.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Please allow me to express my gratitude once again, Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hehe, pleasure. Well, I've given you all the help I can. The rest is up to you... Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We won't let you down.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah. We aren't about to lose!

talks.objective: Talk to Nahida

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... how are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's a teensy bit nervous... but only a teeny-tiny bit. Seems like she's gotten way braver over the last few years, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Of course. After all the adventures you've had with {NICKNAME}, I'm sure you've gained a lot of experience and grown as a person.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm doing alright. What about you, Nahida? How are you holding up?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: With the negative effects of Irminsul... I'm a bit like a piece of fruit that's been burrowed into by hungry insects and left to rot. I'd be lying if I said it was nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But please, don't worry. We all know what we're getting into, and we've prepared as well as we can. I believe in everyone, I believe in you, and I believe in myself.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Stoking the fire inside oneself is certainly one way to live, but knowing when to rely on one's companions is also a form of great wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehe. I've been quietly learning little things from everyone, like plucking tufts of fur from a Sumpter Beast.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Me too. With the constant traveling, I'm always learning and growing. That's the journey of life.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I think there's someone else here who would share that sentiment.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Don't worry about what I think. I was just passing by and happened to overhear your conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you talking about, Hat Guy? This is the top floor! No one "passes by" the top floor!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Says who? You can fly just like I can. I would have thought it makes sense to you of all people.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...I don't know why, but I feel a little more relaxed now.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It shows that you feel comfortable laying down your burdens in our presence. It means that Sumeru is a place you can trust, where you know we have your back.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: And we feel exactly the same way around you. That's what it means to be friends.

talks.objective: Take a walk around and see what everyone's talking about

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Mausoleum of King Deshret, Upper Level

talks.objective: Get some rest so you'll be ready for the next day

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Rest For the Night

talks.objective: Take a walk around and see what everyone's talking about

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We'll make our move after sunrise tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Good. Is everything ready?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: As much as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That'll be enough. Don't let the pressure get to you. We'll take things one step at a time. That's how we've always done it.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Master Tighnari, Mr. Cyno, so this is where you were.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I brought some juice and some water. Would you like some?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I know how easily you get dehydrated in the desert, so you should definitely have some water. In which case, I'll have the juice.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I gotta ask though... who's on juice-making duty at a time like this?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Madam Faruzan said she was feeling a little nervous, so I told her about the automatic juicer my friend invented. She took it right off me and started making carton after carton of juice.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: A juicer? Did Sucrose send that to you?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah. I hadn't had the chance to try it out before this incident occurred... But I couldn't bear to leave it behind in Gandharva Ville.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The juice is very sweet.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I think so too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Collei, how are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Physically, I'm okay. But...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...It just still feels strange to me. Why would a great power like this come to someone like me?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I know the feeling well. That same question ran through my mind every day as a kid.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: At least now, you have someone who can relate to you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: All the more reason that you should apply for Spantamad. Tighnari fiercely opposes the idea, though.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Those two things are completely unrelated.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: What are we all chatting about, hmm? Would anyone like any juice? Oh, you have some already...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I had some earlier, Ma'am. Maybe give the extra to someone else?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Very well, very well. I shall be off then.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's this enormous power, and then there's little old you. You feel like there's no connection between the two, and that sense of dissonance is difficult to get used to.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: *sigh* Yeah... But after all this time, I can't believe this stuff still gets to me sometimes. Makes me feel a little childish...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei, just because we normally keep the conversation light doesn't mean we can't discuss deeper issues.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I don't think it's childish at all. You were the victim of a terrible crime. It's normal to struggle with the fallout from it. You have absolutely nothing to be ashamed of.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: My professor once told me that no incident can be considered truly resolved until the victim says it's over.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Your rage and your pain are completely justified.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Miss Nicole said that... the same god remains which were once used to inflict so much pain upon me have now become a weapon with which I can protect everyone. It's like my own personal kind of evolution.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Every innocent person who's been hurt needs time to realize that it wasn't their fault. I was the same.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But it's all about to be over... Tomorrow, it ends for good.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I don't know if you've noticed, but you rarely stumble over your words anymore, and your outlook has become much more positive. It's a big change from how you used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And since this isn't over, you can settle the matter on your own terms. It's time you seized back control. I believe in you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah. Sumeru is my home, and it's so important to me. I have to protect it... No, I will protect it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And once you're done... how about you come back and apply for Spantamad?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ugh, stop it with the sales pitch, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hey, excuse me! There are still three unclaimed cups of juice here. Why don't you take one each? My arms are getting sore from carrying them around everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Pfft... Madam Faruzan, why are you... Here, let me take them off your hands.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Thank you, Madam Faruzan.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Drink up, and enjoy my handiwork. I think I'm going to make something else now instead.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Please, try to relax, Madam Faruzan! Your nerves are starting to get the better of you...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I know, I know... Ugh.

talks.objective: Take a walk around and see what everyone's talking about

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Too bad we've got a fight tomorrow. I could really do with a stiff drink.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Let us pray instead.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Prayer... Ah, how nostalgic.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Lord Sangemah Bay. Came to get some fresh air too, did'ja?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: That's right! Actually, I was hoping I might run in to you, Dehya. I wanted to let you know that I've stocked up on that perfume you said you were so fond of.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, really? I'll take two. Any chance of a friends and family discount...?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Heh, I knew you'd ask that, and I'm afraid to say that...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Surprise! It's free of charge!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: That's very generous of you, Lord Sangemah Bay. Does this mean you've made a fortune in Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Nope! Turns out, it's not that easy to turn a profit there. I even ran some assorted losses... But anyway, that has nothing to do with why I wanted to give you and Dehya a small gift.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Remember that merchant caravan you two rescued in the desert last month? That was transporting my goods!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, no way! I had no idea that was your shipment. Explains the, uh, eclectic mix of goods though.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Lord Sangemah Bay's investment in the desert and generous stockpiling of goods has helped many people over the years. The shelters you funded, especially, have made life a little easier for the children and the elderly.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: W—Wait, how did you know about that!? ...Oh, I see. Nefer told you, didn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Gah... That pesky lady! Aren't intel brokers at least supposed to charge for divulging people's secrets!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah, she and Candace go way back. It's normal for close friends to share things you wouldn't tell to everyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Sure, but why did they have to be things about me!?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: That's how Nefer shows that she cares. She wishes for all of us to know what a generous person you truly are.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It must be hard trying to make a living far away from home. Just because we can tell what kind of person you are doesn't mean everyone else can.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Well, maybe her intentions were partly good, but I don't think that's the full story. I'm sure she enjoyed knowing how much it would annoy me... I'm telling you, Nefer's got a mean streak.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Definitely with you on that.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Does praying help you stay calm?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Defending one's home is a just cause. My heart is filled with a mix of anger and hope.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Anger... You know, being able to get angry is a good thing. It shows that you're in touch with the real world, and that you have the passion to pursue something you believe in.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm? My lady? what are you doing out here?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Just taking a walk to clear my head, and look where I ended up... Were you praying just now?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes, Miss Dunyarzad. Would you like to join us?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Come on, it's fine. She won't mind who you pray to.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh... Then, sure.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I remember you, Miss Dunyarzad! You've visited my shop before. If I recall correctly, the god you worship is the Dendro Archon, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: That's right. She is such a gentle and kind god. But to me... she is more than just a god I worship.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I see her more as... a friend. And so do many others. She's not some almighty god who reigns on high, but a genuine friend.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Agreed, agreed. She's a wise teacher and a good friend.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I spoke with several people during the evacuation. Everyone's aware that tomorrow's battle is one that ordinary people can join too. A battle to fight for our friends and our homeland.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It makes me glad... I can finally do something for those who protected me.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, you've grown so much since we first met.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh, a compliment? Ooh, more please. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady, you've always been a remarkably strong and ambitious person. It's indisputable. And that's not just a compliment, it's a statement of fact.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What are you praying for?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Our beliefs may not be entirely the same, but we both wish for the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: (I pray that everyone will rise to the challenges ahead and return safe and sound.)

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: (I pray for the safe return of all my companions.)

talks.objective: Take a walk around and see what everyone's talking about

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ahhh! It's finally done... Ugh, but I have a nagging feeling that there's something I've forgotten...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, there you are. Everything wrapped up on your end?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Okay, fair enough — that was a pointless question. We were working in tandem, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You must really be exhausted.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well, it's been a busy day. For both of us.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: When work ends, you clock out. No looking back.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah, we're definitely due a break. Probably a little late to start drinking now, though... I'll stick with water.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Here, this one's for you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You want a bite to eat? I can grab us something. Or wait, I think there's a stove nearby — lemme take a look...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Are you nervous?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...A little, yeah. Unlike you, it seems... How are you not feeling at all nervous?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Because everything that happens next is beyond my individual control. I don't worry about things I cannot influence.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "cannot influence"? You're the one who came up with half of the strategies we ended up using.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There's only so much I can do. I was only doing my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Was it like this last time, too?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You mean, with Azar and his accomplices? ...Yes and no. The situation back then was easier to control, but we weren't as prepared as we are this time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So the enemy is stronger, but so are we.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmph, I still vividly remember the way you interrogated me in the library after the fact... "Where were you when Sumeru needed you most?"

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If your memory is so vivid, you might also recall that it was you who came looking for an argument. You're often the one who initiates these things, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I came for a conversation! I didn't know it was gonna turn into an argument... Anyway, at least I showed up this time. So, what do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What do I think? I think we're certainly better off for it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's good having me around to help out, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Absolutely. As a citizen of Sumeru, you displayed a remarkable sense of responsibility in the face of disaster.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Certainly feels that way. I just shudder to think how the world would've ended up if we hadn't gotten control of the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So, uh... Do you think this is what impending disaster looks like?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: The sky is so clear, and there isn't a whiff of decay or destruction in the air... It's hard to imagine that the fall of humanity could happen on an ordinary day like this.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Awful things happen all the time. Sometimes, people can stop them, and sometimes they can't.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What you and I have done is increase our chances of stopping this one.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ..."Lofty ideals may provide no defense at all against nihilism, but perhaps little decisions can"...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, nothing. It's nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I hope everything works out tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It will. As long as we stick to the plan, our chances of success are good.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh*... It's really strange. You're my junior, yet you always seem to act more like an upperclassman than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I think it's mostly a matter of temperament.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ugh... Walked right into that one, didn't I...

talks.objective: Take a walk around and see what everyone's talking about
Take a walk around and see what everyone's talking about

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Look at the time... I should head back— Ah!

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Oh... I—I'm so sorry, I was in a hurry and didn't look where I was going... Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Wait, you're...

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: ...Have we met?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Not exactly. I think we may have crossed paths by the House of Daena before.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Oh... Ah! You're Hat Guy! From Vahumana, right?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You recognize me?

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: The clue's in the name, Mr. Hat Guy.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Fair point...

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's getting pretty late. What's keeping you up?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I could ask you the same question. If I'm not mistaken, all the workload for the Rtawahist Darshan wrapped up a good while ago.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Well, I have something of a background in Satyavada Life, so I was helping the Dendro Archon make some preparations... But I must have lost track of time.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Did you find the experience enlightening at all?

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Honestly, it was tedious and uneventful at first. But eventually, I think I did sense some profound truths... but they also brought a lot of suffering with them.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: I was told that I even shed tears while I was meditating, though I have no idea why... Sorry, I hope I'm not scaring you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Not at all. It just proves you're very accomplished in your research.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Good night. I wish you all the best for tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Thank you, Sir. You too.

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where to next?

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Mausoleum of King Deshret, Lower Level

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Time to go! Let's go find Nahida!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: These devices should still be usable even though they're broken down. Let's take them back for the others to review.
